title: Australian Trade & Career Pathway Guide 2026
excerpt: A practical overview of selected Australian trade qualifications, occupation references, further-study options and the Job Ready Program pathway.
author: Md Rakibul Islam Sabbir
content:
## About this guide

This guide brings together course-level information and general pathway concepts to help readers explore Australian trade study and career options.

It covers selected Certificate III trade qualifications, course codes and indicative durations, primary ANZSCO occupation references, related employment titles, further-study ideas and a high-level explanation of the Trades Recognition Australia (TRA) Job Ready Program (JRP).

> **Important:** This is general educational information, not migration or legal advice. Course availability, training-package details, occupation classifications, assessment requirements, fees and visa rules can change. Confirm current information with the relevant training provider and Australian authorities.

## ANZSCO occupation reference

ANZSCO codes classify occupations, not simply course names or general job titles. Use the occupation that best matches the actual work performed and check the relevant assessing authority's current requirements.

| Trade area | Employment / occupation title | ANZSCO | How to interpret it |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Wall & Floor Tiling | Tiler | 333411 | Occupational title used by the qualification; the ANZSCO occupation is Wall and Floor Tiler. |
| Wall & Floor Tiling | Wall and Floor Tiler | 333411 | Direct occupation match. |
| Wall & Floor Tiling | Construction Trade Worker | — | Generic title; identify the specific occupation actually performed. |
| Solid Plastering | Solid Plasterer | 333212 | Alternative title; the occupation reference is Renderer (Solid Plaster). |
| Solid Plastering | Renderer | 333212 | Renderer (Solid Plaster). |
| Solid Plastering | Plastering Apprentice | — | Apprentice is an employment status, not a separate occupation code. |
| Bricklaying & Blocklaying | Bricklayer | 331111 | Direct occupation match. |
| Bricklaying & Blocklaying | Blocklayer | 331111* | The guide notes that the qualification includes Blocklayer; it does not identify a separate current code for Blocklayer. |
| Bricklaying & Blocklaying | Paver | 331111* | The guide notes no separate Paver code in this context; confirm classification against actual duties and current sources. |
| Roof Plumbing | Roof Plumber | 334115 | Direct occupation match. |
| Roof Plumbing | Roofing Technician | — | No separate code established in the guide; match the occupation to actual duties. |
| Roof Plumbing | Construction Trade Worker | — | Generic title; no single code. |
| Glass & Glazing | Glazier | 333111 | Direct occupation match. |
| Glass & Glazing | Glass Installer | 333111 | Use the Glazier occupation where duties align. |
| Glass & Glazing | Glazing Tradesperson | 333111 | Use the Glazier occupation where duties align. |
| Glass & Glazing | Construction Glazing Worker | 333111 | Use the Glazier occupation where duties align. |
| Cabinet Making & Timber Technology | Cabinet Maker | 394112 | Direct occupation match. |
| Cabinet Making & Timber Technology | Cabinetmaker | 394111 | Distinct from Cabinet Maker 394112 in the guide's TRA/ANZSCO comparison. |
| Cabinet Making & Timber Technology | Furniture Maker | 394113 | Direct occupation match. |
| Cabinet Making & Timber Technology | Joiner | 331213 | Direct occupation match. |
| Cabinet Making & Timber Technology | Shopfitter | 331211* | The guide describes this as a specialisation under Carpenter and Joiner in ANZSCO 2022; verify the current classification. |
| Cabinet Making & Timber Technology | Wood Machinist | 394213 | Direct occupation match. |
| Carpentry | Carpenter | 331212 | Direct occupation match. |
| Carpentry | Formwork Carpenter | 331212 | Specialisation under Carpenter. |
| Carpentry | Residential / Commercial Carpenter | 331212 | Use Carpenter where duties align with the occupation. |
| Painting & Decorating | Painter | 332211 | Direct occupation match. |
| Painting & Decorating | Painter and Decorator | 332211 | Alternative title under the Painter occupation. |
| Painting & Decorating | Painting Trades Worker | 332211 | The guide uses this occupation reference for the skills-assessment section. |

**Key:** “—” means the guide does not assign a separate ANZSCO code to that generic or employment-status title. An asterisk indicates a qualification/occupation-context note in the source guide. Confirm all codes and classifications against current official references before relying on them.

## The student pathway

A general sequence from trade study to skills recognition and then exploring future options is outlined below. Each step has its own eligibility requirements.

1. **Study:** Choose and complete an appropriate trade qualification.
2. **Qualification completed:** Gain the Australian trade qualification.
3. **Provisional Skills Assessment (PSA):** Apply for a PSA if eligible and required for the intended pathway.
4. **Successful PSA:** The guide states that a successful PSA is required before starting the Job Ready Program.
5. **TRA Job Ready Program:** Complete the relevant JRE, JRWA and JRFA stages, subject to current program rules.
6. **Official skills assessment outcome:** After successful completion, TRA issues an official Skills Assessment Outcome Letter.
7. **Check eligibility:** Review the intended visa pathway, occupation requirements and current criteria.
8. **Expression of Interest (EOI):** If eligible for a points-tested pathway, consider an EOI through SkillSelect.
9. **Invitation:** If invited, review the invitation requirements and prepare the relevant application.
10. **Visa application:** Lodge the relevant application only if invited and eligible.

> **There is no guaranteed outcome.** Completing a course or skills assessment does not itself guarantee employment, an invitation, visa approval or permanent residency.

### Further-study ideas listed in the guide

- Certificate IV and Diploma-level building and construction qualifications.
- Certificate IV in Plumbing for relevant roof-plumbing pathways.
- Certificate IV in Glass and Glazing, Building and Construction, or advanced trade and supervisory pathways.
- Furniture design and manufacturing, kitchen and bathroom design, and related diploma or advanced design pathways for cabinet-making students.
- Further construction management and related study pathways.

## TRA Job Ready Program (JRP)

The guide describes the JRP as a minimum 12-month employment-based skills assessment for eligible international student graduates of an Australian VET course who are working in Australia. It is intended to assess applied skills against Australian standards in the nominated occupation.

### Before starting

The guide states that a Provisional Skills Assessment (PSA) completed within the previous three years and a successful PSA are required before starting the Program. Check the current TRA guidelines for eligibility and any exceptions.

### The three official stages

| Stage | Purpose described in the guide | Indicative timing in the guide |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Job Ready Employment (JRE)** | Checks eligibility, registers the participant and allows them to gain experience and develop skills in an Australian workplace. | Registration may take up to 30 days. |
| **Job Ready Workplace Assessment (JRWA)** | An approved RTO assessor assesses the participant's ability to work at the required skill level in the nominated occupation, at the workplace. | Completion may take up to 15 weeks. |
| **Job Ready Final Assessment (JRFA)** | The final stage after successful completion of prior steps and the required 12-month Employment Confirmation Form. | TRA issues the official outcome letter after successful completion. |

### Key requirements and timing stated in the guide

- Minimum 12 months of full-time or equivalent employment, unless eligible prior employment applies.
- An average of 38 hours or more per week is treated as full-time in the guide; less is calculated pro rata.
- The Program must be completed within three years from the Start Date.
- Participants must continue working in the nominated occupation to complete the minimum employment requirement.

### Program fees shown in the May 2026 guide

- **JRE:** AUD $490
- **JRWA:** AUD $2,845
- **JRFA:** AUD $75
- **Total:** AUD $3,410

Additional JRWA fees may apply if another workplace assessment is required. Fees can change, so check the current TRA fee schedule before applying.

### Final outcome

The guide states that successful completion of the Job Ready Final Assessment leads to an official Skills Assessment Outcome Letter. It also notes that the letter may be used as formal proof of skills and experience when applying for a skilled visa, where relevant. TRA assessment results do not determine visa eligibility by themselves.

## Sources & verification notes

### Primary JRP source

Trades Recognition Australia (TRA), *Job Ready Program Guidelines — May 2026, Version 37.0*, described in the guide as last updated April 2026.

### Information used

The guide follows the JRE → JRWA → JRFA structure and summarises the minimum 12-month employment requirement, 38-hour full-time benchmark, three-year completion period, JRE registration timeframe, JRWA timeframe and the Skills Assessment Outcome Letter following successful completion.

For official program information, use the [Trades Recognition Australia website](https://www.tradesrecognitionaustralia.gov.au/). For visa information, use the [Australian Department of Home Affairs website](https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/). For occupation classification, check current official ANZSCO resources.
